s: From where did General Bakht Khan, the real military leader of the rebels at Delhi, come to Delhi?
x: Bakht Khan came from Bareilly, reaching Delhi on 3 July 1857, and led a 10-member 'Court of Soldiers' there.

s: Begum Hazrat Mahal of Lucknow declared whom the ruler of Awadh in 1857?
x: Begum Hazrat Mahal led the revolt at Lucknow and proclaimed her son Birjis Qadr ruler of Awadh.

s: In which region did Tantia Tope mainly lead the Revolt of 1857?
x: Tantia Tope operated in Central India; Kunwar Singh led in Bihar, Begum Hazrat Mahal in Awadh and Bakht Khan at Delhi.

s: Which of the following pairs (leader of 1857 – centre) is correctly matched?
x: Kunwar Singh led at Arrah (Bihar); Hazrat Mahal led at Lucknow, Nana Saheb at Kanpur and Bahadur Shah Zafar at Delhi.

s: What title did Khan Bahadur Khan, who led the revolt at Bareilly, take for himself?
x: Khan Bahadur Khan proclaimed himself Nawab Nizam at Bareilly and commanded an army of about 40,000.

s: Who was the real military leader of the rebels at Delhi in 1857?
x: Bahadur Shah II was only the nominal leader at Delhi; General Bakht Khan was the real military leader.

s: How many members were in the 'Court of Soldiers' led by General Bakht Khan at Delhi?
x: Bakht Khan, who reached Delhi from Bareilly on 3 July 1857, led a 10-member 'Court of Soldiers'.

s: About how large was the army of Khan Bahadur Khan at Bareilly?
x: Khan Bahadur Khan of Bareilly proclaimed himself Nawab Nizam and had an army of about 40,000.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a leader of the Revolt of 1857?
x: Bhagat Singh belongs to the later freedom movement and only drew on 1857's legacy (APPSC 2019 odd one out). Maulvi Ahmadullah led at Faizabad, Khan Bahadur Khan at Bareilly, and Maulvi Liyakat Ali at Allahabad and Banaras.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Birsa Munda was associated with the Munda Ulgulan.
2. Sidhu and Kanhu were associated with the Santhal Rebellion.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Birsa Munda led the Ulgulan of 1899–1900 and Sidhu and Kanhu led the Santhal Rebellion of 1855–56.

s: Where did Thakur Kushal Singh, who beat the British-Jodhpur army in 1857, lead the revolt?
x: Thakur Kushal Singh of Auwa in Rajputana beat the British-Jodhpur army in 1857.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Leader)
A. Kunwar Singh
B. Begum Hazrat Mahal
C. Khan Bahadur Khan
D. Maulvi Liyaqat Ali
List-II (Centre)
1. Bareilly
2. Arrah
3. Allahabad
4. Lucknow
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Kunwar Singh led at Arrah, Hazrat Mahal at Lucknow, Khan Bahadur Khan at Bareilly and Maulvi Liyaqat Ali at Allahabad.

s: Who led the Revolt of 1857 in Assam?
x: Maniram Dewan (Dutt) led the revolt in Assam.

s: Which of the following pairs (leader – region of 1857) is correctly matched?
x: Maniram Dewan led the revolt in Assam; Kushal Singh was at Auwa, Shah Mal at Baraut and Liyaqat Ali at Allahabad.

s: Who captured Gwalior from the Scindia in 1858?
o: Begum Hazrat Mahal and Birjis Qadr
x: Tantia Tope and Rani Lakshmibai captured Gwalior; Scindia fled to Agra.

s: Who made Khan Bahadur Khan the Viceroy of Rohilkhand?
x: Bahadur Shah II made Khan Bahadur Khan, leader at Bareilly, Viceroy of Rohilkhand.

s: Where did Maulvi Ahmadullah lead the Revolt of 1857?
x: Ahmadullah operated in Faizabad; Khan Bahadur Khan was in Rohilkhand, Kunwar Singh in Bihar and Tantia Tope in Central India.

s: Shah Mal mobilised the headmen and cultivators of which area during the Revolt of 1857?
o: The chaurasee des of 84 villages in Baraut
x: Shah Mal mobilised the chaurasee des, meaning the area of 84 villages, in the Baraut region of Uttar Pradesh.

s: Where did Uda Devi fight against the British in 1857?
x: Uda Devi fought at Sikandar Bagh in Lucknow; Jhalkari Bai is linked with Jhansi and Azizun with Kanpur.

s: Where did Jhalkari Bai, the lookalike of Rani Lakshmibai, fight in 1857?
x: Jhalkari Bai, Lakshmibai's lookalike, commanded the women's wing at Jhansi.

s: Which of the following pairs (local leader – centre) is correctly matched?
x: Azizun was active at Kanpur; Uda Devi fought at Lucknow, Jhalkari Bai at Jhansi and Shah Mal at Baraut.

s: Who among the following was the correspondent of The Times who reported on the Revolt of 1857 and British reprisals?
x: W. H. Russell, correspondent of The Times, reported on the revolt and British reprisals in My Diary in India.

s: Azimullah Khan went to London primarily to plead which case?
o: The restoration of the Nizam’s authority
The pension case of Nana Saheb
The forest-produce rights of Savara chiefs
x: Azimullah Khan, Nana Saheb’s adviser, went to London to plead Nana Saheb’s pension case.

s: In which work did W.H. Russell record the revolt and British revenge?
x: W.H. Russell, correspondent of The Times, reported the revolt and British revenge in 'My Diary in India'.

s: What was the original name of Tantia Tope, commander-in-chief of Nana Saheb?
x: Tantia Tope, Nana Saheb's commander-in-chief, was originally named Ramachandra Pandurang.

s: Who among the following was called 'Krantidoot'?
x: Azimullah Khan, adviser and secretary of Nana Saheb, who went to London for Nana's pension case, was called 'Krantidoot'.

s: Where was Rani Lakshmibai killed in battle on 17 June 1858?
x: Rani Lakshmibai was killed fighting at Kotah-ki-Serai near Gwalior on 17 June 1858.

s: Where was Rani Lakshmibai born?
x: Rani Lakshmibai was born at Kashi (Banaras).

s: Where did Rani Avantibai Lodhi of Ramgarh defeat Waddington in 1857?
x: Rani Avantibai Lodhi of Ramgarh beat Waddington at Kheri near Mandla and died in 1858.

s: On which date was Nana Saheb proclaimed Peshwa at Kanpur?
x: Nana Saheb was proclaimed Peshwa at Kanpur on 5 June 1857.

s: On which date did the Mangal Pandey incident at Barrackpore occur?
x: Mangal Pandey attacked British officers at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857.

s: What was the slogan of the Meerut rebels when they marched in May 1857?
x: After 85 sepoys of the 3rd (Light) Cavalry were jailed, the rebels freed the prisoners and marched to Delhi with the slogan 'Dilli Chalo'.

s: Whom did the rebels at Delhi kill after entering the Red Fort in May 1857?
x: After reaching Delhi, the rebels entered the Red Fort and killed Commissioner Simon Fraser.

s: To which regiment did Mangal Pandey, who attacked Lt Baugh at Barrackpore, belong?
x: Mangal Pandey of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry attacked Lt Baugh at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857; the 3rd Cavalry rose later at Meerut.

s: How many sepoys of the 3rd Cavalry were sentenced at Meerut on 9 May 1857 for refusing the cartridges?
x: On 9 May 1857, 85 sepoys of the 3rd (Bengal Light) Cavalry at Meerut were sentenced to 10 years for refusing the cartridges.

s: On which date was Mangal Pandey hanged?
x: Mangal Pandey was hanged on 8 April 1857 and the 34th BNI was disbanded; 29 March was the day of his attack.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Revolt of 1857:
1. The first outbreak took place at Barrackpore.
2. The real start of the revolt was at Meerut on 10 May 1857.
3. The rebels reached Delhi on 11 May 1857.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Mangal Pandey's outbreak at Barrackpore (29 March) came first; the revolt proper began at Meerut on 10 May and the rebels reached Delhi on 11 May.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched (centre – date the rising began, 1857)?
x: The rising at Kanpur began on 5 June 1857, not 11 May; 11 May is the date the rebels reached Delhi.

s: On which date did the rising at Kanpur, where Nana Saheb was proclaimed Peshwa, begin?
x: Nana Saheb was proclaimed Peshwa at Kanpur on 5 June 1857, the day the rising there began; Lucknow rose fully on 4 June.

s: Which of the following areas rose in October 1857?
x: The Kolhapur area rose in October 1857; Gwalior rose in June and Indore in July 1857.

s: When did the rising at Jhansi begin?
x: The rising at Jhansi began in June 1857, not on 11 May, which was the day the rebels reached Delhi.

s: Which of the following areas rose in July 1857?
x: Indore, Mhow, Sagar, Jhelum and Sialkot rose in July 1857.

s: From where did General Bakht Khan, who commanded the defence of Delhi in 1857, come to Delhi?
x: Bakht Khan came from Bareilly and reached Delhi on 3 July 1857 (APPSC-GS 2023 key). Lucknow was Begum Hazrat Mahal's centre, Kanpur Nana Saheb's, and Faizabad Maulvi Ahmadullah's.

s: Where was Bahadur Shah Zafar exiled after the Revolt of 1857?
x: After Delhi fell, Bahadur Shah Zafar was tried and exiled to Rangoon (Yangon), where he died in 1862.

s: In which year did Bahadur Shah Zafar die in exile at Rangoon?
x: The last Mughal emperor died at Rangoon in 1862.

s: When was Bareilly recaptured by the British?
x: Bareilly was recaptured in May 1858, after Jhansi was retaken in April 1858.

s: When did Colin Campbell recapture Lucknow?
x: Campbell retook Kanpur in December 1857 and Lucknow in March 1858; Hugh Rose took Jhansi in April and Gwalior in June 1858.

s: Who recaptured Jhansi in April 1858?
x: Hugh Rose recaptured Jhansi in April 1858 and Gwalior in June 1858.

s: Who first recaptured Kanpur on 16 July 1857?
x: Henry Havelock first recaptured Kanpur on 16 July 1857; Colin Campbell retook it in December 1857.

s: Who carried out the first relief of Lucknow on 25 September 1857?
x: Havelock, with Outram, made the first relief of Lucknow on 25 September 1857.

s: Who recaptured Gwalior from the rebels in June 1858?
x: Hugh Rose retook Jhansi (April 1858) and Gwalior (June 1858).

s: Whose help did Colin Campbell have in recapturing Lucknow in March 1858?
x: Colin Campbell recaptured Lucknow in March 1858 with Gorkha help.

s: Which British general died at Lucknow on 24 November 1857?
x: Havelock died at Lucknow on 24 November 1857; Nicholson fell at Delhi.

s: Where was Tantia Tope hanged on 18 April 1859?
x: Tantia Tope was betrayed, captured and hanged at Shivpuri on 18 April 1859, the last major leader executed.

s: Where did Kunwar Singh die on 26 April 1858?
x: Kunwar Singh was wounded crossing the Ganga and died at Jagdishpur on 26 April 1858.

s:
Consider the following statements about the fate of rebel leaders:
1. Nana Saheb escaped to Nepal.
2. Begum Hazrat Mahal escaped to Nepal.
3. Tantia Tope escaped to Nepal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Nana Saheb and Begum Hazrat Mahal escaped to Nepal; Tantia Tope was captured and executed in 1859.

s: Who was the last major leader of the Revolt of 1857 to be executed?
x: Tantia Tope is regarded as the last major leader of the Revolt of 1857 to be executed.

s: Which British officer died defending the Lucknow Residency in 1857?
x: Sir Henry Lawrence died defending the Residency at Lucknow; Nicholson fell at Delhi.

s: The Revolt of 1857 was mainly centred in which region?
x: The Revolt of 1857 was centred in North and Central India. Bengal is linked to the Sanyasi-Fakir revolt, Chotanagpur to the Kol revolt and Andhra to the Rampa revolt.

s: Which of the following regions formed the main zone of the Revolt of 1857?
o: The Doab, Awadh, Rohilkhand, Bihar, Bundelkhand and Central India
Eastern, western and southern coastal India
x: The main zone included the Doab, Awadh, Rohilkhand, Bihar, Bundelkhand and Central India.

s: Which of the following regions was largely unaffected by the Revolt of 1857?
o: Bengal, Punjab, eastern, western and southern India
x: Bengal, Punjab, and eastern, western and southern India were largely unaffected; British forces for suppression came from several of these regions.

s: To which place did Scindia of Gwalior, whose troops went over to the Rani, flee in 1857?
x: Scindia stayed loyal to the British, but his troops defected to the Rani and he fled to Agra.

s: In which pair of states did the troops rebel in 1857 while the rulers stayed loyal?
x: At Tonk and Bhopal the troops rebelled but the rulers stayed loyal; Jaipur and Chittor were not centres of the revolt.

s: Which Rajputana centre saw a sepoy rising in May 1857?
x: Nasirabad saw a sepoy rising in May 1857; the rising at Neemuch came in June 1857.

s: Which of the following rulers stayed loyal to the British during the Revolt of 1857?
x: The Nizam of Hyderabad, Mysore, Scindia and Holkar stayed loyal to the British.

s: In which Rajputana state did the troops rise against their own ruler in 1857?
x: At Kota the troops rose against the ruler; at Tonk and Bhopal the troops rebelled but the rulers stayed loyal.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Hindu-Muslim unity of 1857:
1. It was later cited against the two-nation theory.
2. It was later cited in support of the Doctrine of Lapse.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Hindu-Muslim unity of the revolt was later cited against the two-nation theory; it had nothing to do with the Doctrine of Lapse.

s: What title did the rebels at Delhi give to Bahadur Shah II?
x: The rebels at Delhi proclaimed Bahadur Shah II 'Shahenshah-e-Hindustan'; Nawab Nizam was the title of Khan Bahadur Khan.

s: What was the pension of Bahadur Shah Zafar?
x: Bahadur Shah Zafar's pension was one lakh rupees a month (Rs 99,000 in Delhi and Rs 1,000 in Lucknow).

s: Which Nizam of Hyderabad remained pro-British during the Revolt of 1857?
x: Afzal-ud-Daula remained pro-British, and his loyalty helped keep the Deccan quiet.

s: The two principal local risings in Andhra associated with the Revolt of 1857 occurred at which pair of places?
x: Dandasena led the rising at Paralakimidi, while Korukonda Subba Reddy led the rebellion at Errannagudem; both occurred in August 1857.

s: Dandasena, the Savara chief associated with the Revolt of 1857, rose at Paralakimidi after which development?
o: The ban on selling forest produce
The removal of the Nizam from Hyderabad
x: Dandasena rose at Paralakimidi on 9 August 1857 after the ban on selling forest produce.

s:
With reference to Hyderabad during the Revolt of 1857, consider the following statements:
1. Nizam Afzal-ud-Daula joined the rebels against the British.
2. Mubariz-ud-Daula's imprisonment in Golconda came before Turrebaz Khan's attack on the Residency.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: Only statement 2 is correct: Mubariz-ud-Daula was imprisoned in Golconda before Turrebaz Khan's attack on the Residency. Statement 1 is wrong because Nizam Afzal-ud-Daula stayed pro-British.

s: On which date did Turrebaz Khan lead the attack on the British Residency at Hyderabad?
x: Turrebaz Khan, with Maulvi Allauddin, attacked the Hyderabad Residency from the Mecca Masjid on 17 July 1857.

s: Sheikh Peer Shah, imprisoned for secret contact with sepoys in 1857, was from:
x: Sheikh Peer Shah of Cuddapah (Rayalaseema) had secret contact with the Cuddapah sepoys and was imprisoned.

s: Who was imprisoned in Golconda before Turrebaz Khan's attack on the Hyderabad Residency?
x: Mubariz-ud-Daula was imprisoned in Golconda before Turrebaz Khan's attack; Nizam Afzal-ud-Daula stayed pro-British.

s: Where did Korukonda Subba Reddy lead a rebellion in August 1857?
x: Korukonda Subba Reddy rebelled at Errannagudem in August 1857; Paralakimidi was Dandasena's rising.

s: From which mosque did Turrebaz Khan's men set out to attack the British Residency at Hyderabad in 1857?
x: On 17 July 1857 Turrebaz Khan and Maulvi Allauddin led the attack on the Residency from the Mecca Masjid.

s: Who was associated with Turrebaz Khan in the attack on the British Residency at Hyderabad in 1857?
x: Turrebaz Khan attacked the Residency along with Maulvi Allauddin; Mubariz-ud-Daula was already imprisoned in Golconda.

s: Dandasena, who rose at Paralakimidi in 1857, was a chief of which tribe?
x: Dandasena was a Savara chief of Paralakimidi (then Ganjam district).

s: Who crushed the rising of Dandasena at Paralakimidi in 1857?
x: Dandasena's rising was crushed by Capt. Wilson and Dandasena was hanged.

s: On which date did the rebel attack on the Hyderabad Residency, which was repulsed, take place?
x: The attack on the Hyderabad Residency on 17 July 1857 was repulsed, as the Nizam Afzal-ud-Daula and Salar Jung I stayed loyal.

s: Which of the following was a major limitation of the Revolt of 1857?
o: Participation of all major princes and urban elites
Superior arms in the hands of the rebels
Lack of coordination and central leadership
x: The revolt suffered from lack of coordination and central leadership; many big princes and urban elites stayed away, and the rebels had inferior arms and no unified programme.

s: What title was given to the Governor-General under the Government of India Act 1858?
x: The Government of India Act 1858 gave power to the Crown, created a Secretary of State and made the Governor-General the Viceroy.

s: Which of the following was created by the Government of India Act, 1858?
o: The post of Secretary of State for India
x: The 1858 Act moved power to the Crown, created the Secretary of State for India and made the Governor-General the Viceroy.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Indian classes during the Revolt of 1857?
o: The educated middle class remained neutral
The educated middle class led the rising at Delhi
Big zamindars and moneylenders protected their class interests
Merchants and the urban elite gave no support
x: The educated middle class remained neutral, seeing the revolt as a backward-looking feudal reaction; it did not lead any rising.

s: The military disadvantage of the rebels was mainly due to their dependence on which weapons?
x: The rebels generally used swords, spears and old muskets, whereas the British had Enfield rifles and the electric telegraph.

s: Which one of the following regions was largely peaceful during the revolt of 1857?
x: The revolt was concentrated mainly in North and Central India, while Bengal, Madras and Bombay regions remained largely peaceful.

s: Which of the following was a reason for the failure of the Revolt of 1857?
x: The revolt lacked an all-India character and a unified nationalist programme; the rebels had inferior arms and poor communication.

s: Which one of the following combinations contributed to the failure of the revolt of 1857?
o: A common programme for a future society
Unified central command, modern weapons and telegraph communication among rebels
Complete participation of East, West and South India
Loyal princes, loyal big zamindars and inadequate support from the martial races of the north
x: The revolt suffered because several princes and big zamindars remained loyal and it lacked adequate support from the martial races of the north.

s: British troops returning from which war strengthened the suppression of 1857?
x: Troops returning from the Crimea and experienced generals strengthened the British against the rebels.

s: With whom did the Begum of Awadh quarrel, weakening rebel unity in Awadh?
x: Quarrels such as that between the Begum of Awadh and Maulvi Ahmadullah weakened rebel unity.

s: The Revolt of 1857 was chiefly a revolt of which army?
x: The revolt was chiefly of the Bengal Army; the Madras and Bombay armies largely remained loyal, while a Gorkha regiment assisted Campbell.

s: The loyal princes were described as “breakwaters to the storm” by:
x: Lord Canning called the loyal princes "breakwaters to the storm", because they kept their states quiet and helped the British during the revolt.

s: Which of the following pairs regarding 1857 is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Holkar of Indore – Supported the British
Nizam Afzal-ud-Daula and Salar Jung I – Kept the Deccan quiet
Sikh chiefs of Patiala, Nabha and Jind – Actively helped the British
Bhonsle state of Nagpur – Joined the revolt under its ruling prince
x: Nagpur had already been annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse in 1854, so there was no ruling prince to join the revolt.

s: In which year was Nagpur (Bhonsle) annexed, leaving it no ruler to join the revolt?
x: Nagpur (Bhonsle) had already been annexed in 1854, so there was no ruler to join the revolt.

s: Which presidency armies remained loyal to the British in 1857?
x: The revolt was chiefly of the Bengal Army; the Madras and Bombay armies stayed loyal.

s: Which ruler is described as the most loyal to the British during the Revolt of 1857?
x: Scindia of Gwalior stayed most loyal, though his troops joined the Rani.

s: Which troops helped Colin Campbell during the suppression of the revolt?
x: Gorkhas helped Campbell; the revolt was chiefly of the Bengal Army.

s: How did the educated middle class, which generally remained neutral, view the revolt?
o: A movement led by urban merchants
x: The educated middle class generally saw the revolt as a backward-looking feudal reaction and therefore remained neutral.

s: Which group acted as 'breakwaters' in 1857 to protect its class interests?
x: Big zamindars and moneylenders acted as 'breakwaters' to protect their class interests.

s: Who was Governor-General during the Revolt of 1857 and read out the Queen's Proclamation at Allahabad in 1858?
x: Lord Canning was Governor-General during the revolt and, as the first Viceroy, read out the Queen's Proclamation of 1858 at Allahabad.

s: Who became Commander-in-Chief in 1857 after General Anson died?
x: Sir Colin Campbell became Commander-in-Chief after General Anson died in 1857.

s: On which date did Lord Canning formally declare peace after the revolt?
x: Lord Canning declared peace on 8 July 1858; 1 November 1858 was the date of the Queen's Proclamation.

s: By what title was Sir Colin Campbell later known?
x: Sir Colin Campbell, the Commander-in-Chief who retook Lucknow, was later Lord Clyde.

s: Which British officer is associated with the recapture of Delhi in September 1857?
x: John Nicholson was associated with the recapture of Delhi in September 1857 and was killed in the assault.

s: Allahabad and Banaras were associated with the rebellion led by ______ and were recaptured by ______.
x: Maulvi Liyakat Ali led the rebellion at Allahabad and Banaras, which were recaptured by Colonel Neill.

s: Who among the following coordinated communication among rebel leaders while serving as an adviser to Nana Saheb?
x: Azimullah Khan served as Nana Saheb's adviser and coordinated communication among rebel leaders.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Bihar was associated with Kunwar Singh and was recaptured by William Taylor. John Nicholson was associated with the recapture of Delhi.

s: Who suppressed the revolt of Kunwar Singh in Bihar?
x: William Taylor suppressed the revolt of Kunwar Singh in Bihar; Colonel Neill retook Allahabad and Banaras.

s: Which British officer was killed in the assault on Delhi in 1857?
x: John Nicholson was killed leading the assault on Delhi; Lawrence, Neill and Havelock fell at Lucknow.

s: Who captured Bahadur Shah II after the fall of Delhi?
x: Hodson captured the emperor and also shot his sons.

s: Which British general had surrendered at Kanpur before it was retaken by Colin Campbell?
x: General Wheeler had surrendered at Kanpur earlier; Campbell retook Kanpur in December 1857.

s: What finally happened to Bahadur Shah II, the nominal leader of the revolt at Delhi?
o: Killed in the assault on Delhi
Executed at Delhi after a public trial
Captured, tried and exiled to Rangoon
x: Bahadur Shah II was captured, tried and exiled to Rangoon in Burma, where he died in 1862.

s: By whom was Tantia Tope betrayed before he was captured and executed?
x: Tantia Tope was betrayed by Man Singh, captured and executed in April 1859.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kunwar Singh — Took refuge at Agra
Begum Hazrat Mahal — Executed at Kanpur
x: Nana Saheb, the leader at Kanpur, escaped to Nepal. Tantia Tope was executed, Kunwar Singh died in Bihar, and Begum Hazrat Mahal fled to Nepal.

s: After the recapture of Delhi, which of the following occurred?
o: Bahadur Shah was restored and his sons were pardoned.
Bahadur Shah was tried and deported, while his sons were shot by Hodson.
The Mughal line was strengthened under Birjis Qadir.
Bahadur Shah escaped to Nepal with Nana Saheb.
x: After Delhi was recaptured, Bahadur Shah was tried and deported, and his sons were shot by Hodson. The Mughal line consequently ended.

s: In which year did Jhansi, the state of Rani Lakshmibai, lapse to the British?
x: Jhansi lapsed to the British in 1854; Rani Lakshmibai was the widow of Gangadhar Rao.

s: Which of the following pairs (leader – fate) is correctly matched?
o: Rani Lakshmibai – Died fighting Hugh Rose near Gwalior
Bahadur Shah II – Exiled to the Andaman Islands
x: Rani Lakshmibai died near Gwalior fighting Hugh Rose; Tantia Tope was executed, Bahadur Shah was exiled to Rangoon and Kunwar Singh died in Bihar.

s: On which date did Rani Lakshmibai die fighting near Gwalior?
x: Rani Lakshmibai fell near Gwalior on 17 June 1858; 18 April 1859 is Tantia Tope's execution.

s: Rani Lakshmibai was the widow of which ruler of Jhansi?
x: Rani Lakshmibai was the widow of Gangadhar Rao; Damodar Rao was their adopted son.

s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the repression after the suppression of the revolt?
o: Only rebel leaders were fined, while ordinary rebels were released.
Rebels were generally pardoned without trial.
The British avoided punitive measures in Delhi.
Thousands of rebels were publicly executed after mock trials.
x: The repression was harsh; thousands of rebels were publicly executed after mock trials, and British troops also committed atrocities.

s: Who shot the sons of Bahadur Shah II after the fall of Delhi?
x: After Delhi fell, Hodson captured Bahadur Shah II and shot his sons, ending the Mughal line.

s: How did R.C. Majumdar, unlike the nationalist school, describe the Revolt of 1857?
o: the first, national and completely successful war of independence
only a conflict between civilisation and barbarism
neither first, nor national, nor a war of independence
x: R.C. Majumdar's own verdict was that the revolt was neither the first nor national nor a war of independence, despite some classifications placing him in a broader nationalist school.

s: Which of the following pairs (historian – view of 1857) is correctly matched?
o: R.C. Majumdar – First War of Independence
Eric Stokes – Many local peasant and elite risings
V.D. Savarkar – A mere sepoy mutiny
x: Eric Stokes, using local agrarian studies, saw the revolt as many peasant and elite risings, not one centrally directed movement.

s: Who said, 'What began as a fight for religion ended as a war of independence'?
x: S.N. Sen concluded that the revolt began as a fight for religion but ultimately developed into a war of independence.

s: Who said that the uprising of 1857 was essentially a feudal rising?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru described the uprising as essentially a feudal rising in The Discovery of India.

s: In which region did Rudrangshu Mukherjee study the resistance of peasants and taluqdars?
x: Rudrangshu Mukherjee studied peasant and taluqdar resistance in Awadh.

s: In which book did Nehru call the Revolt of 1857 essentially a feudal rising?
x: Nehru called the revolt essentially a feudal rising in The Discovery of India.

s: How did R.C. Majumdar and S.N. Sen regard Indian nationalism in the mid-nineteenth century?
x: Both Majumdar and Sen regarded Indian nationalism in the mid-nineteenth century as still embryonic.

s: Which one of the following books was written by R.C. Majumdar?
o: The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857
Civil Rebellion in the Indian Mutinies
x: R.C. Majumdar wrote The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857, published in 1957.

s: Who wrote 'Awadh in Revolt'?
x: 'Awadh in Revolt' was written by Rudrangshu Mukherjee.

s: Which one of the following was identified by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan as the main cause of the revolt of 1857?
o: The decline of the textile industry in Bengal
The annexation of Punjab by the British
The introduction of the Subsidiary Alliance
The absence of Indians in the Legislative Council
x: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan argued that the absence of Indians in the Legislative Council caused the rulers to misunderstand the ruled.

s: Which of the following historians characterised the uprising of 1857 as a purely military outbreak or a mere sepoy mutiny?
x: Sir John Lawrence, along with J.R. Seeley and Charles Raikes, regarded the uprising primarily as a sepoy mutiny and denied it a popular or national character.

s: Who interpreted the Revolt of 1857 as a war of fanatic religionists against Christians?
x: L.E.R. Rees interpreted the revolt as a war of fanatic religionists against Christians.

s: T.R. Holmes described the Revolt of 1857 as a conflict between which of the following?
x: T.R. Holmes saw the revolt as a conflict of civilisation against barbarism.

s: Who asked in the House of Commons in 1857, 'Is it a military mutiny, or is it a national revolt?'
x: Benjamin Disraeli asked in the Commons on 27 July 1857, 'Is it a military mutiny, or is it a national revolt?'

s: In which publication did Karl Marx call the revolt 'in truth a national revolt'?
x: Karl Marx wrote in the New-York Tribune (1857) that what John Bull called a mutiny was in truth a national revolt.

s: How did Sir James Outram and W. Taylor describe the Revolt of 1857?
o: A conspiracy of Muslims exploiting Hindu grievances
A conflict of civilisation and barbarism
A war of fanatic religionists against Christians
x: Outram and Taylor saw the revolt as a Muslim conspiracy that used Hindu grievances; Holmes spoke of civilisation vs barbarism.

s: Who among the following called the Revolt of 1857 a mere sepoy mutiny?
x: Sir John Lawrence, J.R. Seeley and Charles Raikes called it a mere sepoy mutiny; Marx and Disraeli spoke of a national revolt.

s: Why did the educated middle class largely remain aloof from the revolt of 1857?
o: It considered British rule to be modernising.
It was led by the taluqdars of Awadh.
It had already established an independent national government.
It opposed all forms of education introduced by the British.
x: The educated middle class generally remained aloof because it viewed British rule as modernising.

s: Which of the following groups stayed loyal to the British during the Revolt of 1857?
x: The big zamindars of Bengal stayed loyal, while Awadh taluqdars and zamindars, and peasants and artisans of Awadh and western UP, joined the revolt.

s: Annapurnayya, known as ‘Andhra Netaji’, was sentenced to 18 months’ rigorous imprisonment for which of the following?
o: Writing the article *Chicharapidugu* on the revolt of 1857
Supporting the British policy of divide and rule
Organising the RIN revolt at Bombay
x: Annapurnayya received 18 months’ rigorous imprisonment for his article *Chicharapidugu*, which dealt with the revolt of 1857.

s: Which one of the following statements about the Andhra region during the revolt of 1857 is NOT correct?
o: There were attempts at Kadiri and revolts associated with Korukonda Subba Reddy and Dandasena.
Turrebaz Khan was associated with a limited revolt in Hyderabad.
Andhra had no local leaders or limited revolts during the period.
x: The statement that Andhra had no local leaders or limited revolts is incorrect. Turrebaz Khan, the Kadiri attempt, Korukonda Subba Reddy and Dandasena are associated with such activity.

s: Which groups joined the Revolt of 1857 in Awadh and western UP?
o: Bengal zamindars and the urban elite
x: Awadh taluqdars, peasants and artisans joined the revolt in Awadh and western UP, while the big zamindars of Bengal stayed loyal.

s: Which of the following leaders is associated with a rising in the Andhra region during the Revolt of 1857?
x: Korukonda Subba Reddy led a rising in Andhra; Shah Mal (Baraut), Kunwar Singh (Bihar) and Khan Bahadur Khan (Bareilly) were in the north.

s: In which region of present Andhra Pradesh is Kadiri, where an attempt was made to incite rebellion in 1857?
x: Kadiri is a town of Rayalaseema; the 1857 attempt there was one of the sporadic Andhra risings.

s:
Consider the following statements about the failure of the Revolt of 1857:
1. The rebels lacked a common strategy and central organisation.
2. Major rulers of the Rajput states backed the British.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are causes of failure: no common strategy or central organisation, and big rulers such as the Rajput states sided with the British.

s: The term 'Sepoy Mutiny' or 'Indian Mutiny' was predominantly used by which school of historians?
x: British or imperialist historians commonly used the labels Sepoy Mutiny or Indian Mutiny and denied the revolt a national character.

s: Whose role does the feudal-reaction interpretation of the Revolt of 1857 mainly stress?
o: dispossessed princes and taluqdars attempting to restore their lost positions
urban middle classes demanding representative government
European merchants opposing the East India Company
x: The feudal-reaction interpretation highlights dispossessed princes and taluqdars such as Nana Saheb, Lakshmibai and Begum Hazrat Mahal, who sought to recover lost positions.

s:
Consider the following statements about labels for the Revolt of 1857:
1. British historians called it the Sepoy Mutiny.
2. V.D. Savarkar called it the First War of Independence.
3. The feudal-reaction view stresses the role of the educated middle class.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: British historians called it the Sepoy Mutiny and Savarkar the First War of Independence; the feudal-reaction view stresses dispossessed princes and taluqdars, not the educated class.

s: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels' articles on the uprising were compiled under which title?
o: The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857
Civil Rebellion in the Indian Mutinies
The First Indian War of Independence 1857-1859
x: Karl Marx's and Friedrich Engels' articles were compiled as The First Indian War of Independence 1857-1859.

s: Who wrote 'Eighteen Fifty-Seven', the Government of India-commissioned centenary history of the revolt?
x: S.N. Sen's Eighteen Fifty-Seven was the official centenary history; R.C. Majumdar wrote his 1957 work independently after parting with the official project.

s: Who wrote Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind (1859)?
x: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind in 1859; Mirza Ghalib was the poet who witnessed the revolt.

s: Who wrote '1857: The Great Rebellion'?
x: '1857: The Great Rebellion' was written by Ashok Mehta.

s:
Consider the following statements about the centenary histories of 1857:
1. S.N. Sen's 'Eighteen Fifty-Seven' was government-commissioned.
2. R.C. Majumdar's 'The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857' was an independent work.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Sen wrote the official, government-commissioned history in 1957; Majumdar parted with the official project and wrote independently.

s: The Revolt of 1857 was confined largely to which part of India, while most of India remained neutral?
x: The revolt did not spread evenly; it was largely confined to North India, which is one limit of calling it the First War of Independence.

s: The Revolt of 1857 began as which of the following and quickly grew into a popular rebellion?
x: It began among soldiers as a mutiny but quickly drew in rulers, peasants and common people.

s: Which of the following describes the national character of the Revolt of 1857?
o: A traditional uprising of different classes against a common foreign enemy
A modern nationalist movement with a common programme
x: The idea of a single Indian nation-state had not yet emerged; different classes defended local, economic and religious interests against a common foreign enemy.

s: Which of the following expresses the significance of the Revolt of 1857 despite its failure?
o: It shattered the myth of British invincibility and planted the seeds of later nationalism.
It prevented all later nationalist movements.
It immediately ended British rule in India.
It established a modern democratic government throughout India.
x: The revolt damaged the belief in British invincibility and helped create the conditions for later nationalism, although it did not end British rule.

s: In which year did the RIN revolt, to which the 'mutiny or revolt' debate is also applied, begin on HMIS Talwar?
x: The same 'mutiny or revolt?' debate applies to the RIN revolt that began on HMIS Talwar on 18 February 1946.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Hindu-Muslim relations in the Revolt of 1857?
o: Bahadur Shah II was accepted by both Hindu and Muslim rebels
The greased cartridges offended both Hindus and Muslims
The British responded with a policy of divide and rule
The British responded by transferring authority to the Indian National Congress
x: The British answered Hindu-Muslim cooperation with divide and rule; there was no transfer of authority to the Congress.

s: What was the significance of Bahadur Shah II during the revolt of 1857?
o: He led only the sepoys of the Bengal Army.
He was accepted as the symbolic head by Hindu and Muslim rebels.
He represented the educated middle class in the revolt.
He served as the principal British commander in Delhi.
x: Bahadur Shah II was accepted as the symbolic head by both Hindu and Muslim rebels.

s: What did the Queen's Proclamation of 1858 disclaim?
o: The treaties made by the Company
x: The Proclamation disclaimed further annexation of Indian States and placed the administration of India under the Crown.

s: On what basis did the Queen's Proclamation of 1858 promise that appointments to public service would be made?
x: It promised appointment by merit and qualifications without discrimination of race or creed, and that Company treaties with the princes would be honoured.

s: What is the period 1858-1885, when the Queen's Proclamation's promise of equal employment was not kept, known as?
x: 1858-1885 is called the 'Era of Broken Promises': the ICS stayed European-dominated, Kimberley saying an adequate number 'shall always be Europeans'.

s: What is the Queen's Proclamation of 1858 often called?
o: Magna Carta of the Indian people
Magna Carta of the East India Company
x: The Queen’s Proclamation is often called the Magna Carta of the Indian people because of its wide-ranging assurances concerning rulers, religion, public service, property and land rights.

s: To whom was the Queen's Proclamation of 1858 addressed?
o: The Court of Directors of the Company
The Princes, Chiefs and Peoples of India
The sepoys of the Bengal Army
x: The Proclamation, read at Allahabad on 1 November 1858, was addressed to 'the Princes, Chiefs and Peoples of India'.

s: Which promise of the Queen's Proclamation of 1858 was broken?
o: No further annexation of Indian States
Honouring of the Company's treaties with princes
Appointment to public service regardless of race or creed
x: The promise of equal employment by merit was broken as the ICS stayed European-dominated; the promises on annexation and religion were kept.

s: Which event took place at the Allahabad Durbar of 1 November 1858?
o: Queen Victoria was proclaimed Empress of India
The Queen's Proclamation was read out
The Government of India Act, 1858 was passed
Bahadur Shah II was sent into exile
x: Lord Canning read out the Queen's Proclamation at Allahabad on 1 November 1858. Victoria became Empress of India at Delhi in 1877.

s: Who described the Indian princes who stayed loyal in 1857 as 'breakwaters to the storm'?
x: Lord Canning called the princes who stayed loyal in 1857 "breakwaters to the storm".

s: Who withdrew the Doctrine of Lapse and recognised the right of adoption by childless Indian rulers?
x: Lord Canning withdrew the Doctrine of Lapse and recognised adoption rights after 1857. This marked the abandonment of Dalhousie’s annexation policy.

s: After 1857, Indian princes were assured that their states would not ordinarily be annexed, provided they accepted which of the following?
o: Direct rule by the Board of Control
x: The princes kept their states subject to British paramountcy and became subordinate allies of the Crown.

s: Who founded the Madras Native Association (1852)?
x: Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty's Madras Native Association (1852) was the first to petition against non-implementation of the Allahabad Proclamation.

s: Which organisation was the first to petition against the non-implementation of the Queen's Proclamation of 1858?
x: The Madras Native Association (1852), founded by Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty, was the first to petition against the non-implementation of the Allahabad Proclamation.

s: Who was the first Governor-General of India?
x: The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India; the first was William Bentinck.

s: In which year was the East India Company, whose political rule ended under the Act of 1858, formally dissolved?
x: The Government of India Act, 1858 ended the Company's political rule, and the Company was formally dissolved in 1874.

s: When did the British recapture Delhi during the Revolt of 1857?
x: The British retook Delhi in September 1857; the revolt began at Meerut in May 1857 and Lakshmibai died in June 1858.

s: What was the official title of the Government of India Act, 1858?
o: Act for the Political Settlement of India
Act for the Better Administration of India
Act for the Good Government of India
Act for the Regulation of Crown Territories
x: The Government of India Act, 1858 was titled the Act for the Good Government of India.

s: What did the Charter Act of 1833 make the East India Company?
o: an agency of the Crown headed by the Secretary of State
a body subordinate to the Board of Control in commercial matters only
x: The Charter Act of 1833 ended the Company’s remaining commercial functions and made it a purely administrative organisation.

s: Which Act changed the title to Governor-General of India?
x: The Charter Act of 1833 changed the title to Governor-General of India, and William Bentinck was the first holder of that title.

s: Which Act created the title 'Viceroy and Governor-General'?
x: The Government of India Act of 1858 created the title Viceroy and Governor-General. Lord Canning was its first holder.

s: After 1858, in relation to which of the following was the head of the Government of India styled 'Viceroy'?
x: The same office-holder was Viceroy in relation to the princely states and Governor-General in British India.

s: Under the Government of India Act, 1858, through whom were the powers of the British Crown in India exercised?
o: President of the Board of Control
Chairman of the Court of Directors
x: The Act created the office of the Secretary of State for India, through whom the British Crown exercised its powers in India.

s: Who was the first Secretary of State for India under the Government of India Act, 1858?
x: Lord Stanley was the first Secretary of State for India under the new Crown administration.

s: The Council of India created by the Government of India Act, 1858 to advise the Secretary of State had how many members?
x: The Council of India consisted of 15 members and advised the Secretary of State for India.

s: Which Act abolished the Council of India created by the Government of India Act, 1858?
x: The 15-member Council of India in London, which advised the Secretary of State, was abolished by the 1935 Act.

s: Under the Government of India Act, 1858, to whom was the Secretary of State for India responsible?
x: The Secretary of State was a British cabinet minister and member of Parliament, responsible to Parliament; he could issue orders to the Viceroy.

s: Under which of the following Acts did the East India Company remain in place under a system of dual control?
x: Pitt's India Act, 1784 left the Company in place under dual control. Company rule ended only with the Government of India Act, 1858.

s: Lord Canning was the first to hold which of the following titles?
x: The Act of 1858 gave the Governor-General the added title of Viceroy, and Canning was the first Viceroy. The first Governor-General of India was Bentinck.

s: Which title did the rebels of 1857 confer on Bahadur Shah II?
x: The rebels proclaimed him Shahenshah-e-Hindustan; he was later tried and exiled to Rangoon, formally ending Mughal rule.

s: Which of the following pairs about the Telugu regions after the establishment of Crown rule is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Coastal Andhra – Part of the Madras Presidency
Telangana – Separate province administered directly from London
Rayalaseema – Part of the Madras Presidency
Nizam's dominions – Subject to British suzerainty
x: Telangana remained under the Nizam, subject to British suzerainty; it was not a province administered from London.

s: Where did Bahadur Shah II, the last Mughal emperor, die in exile in 1862?
x: Bahadur Shah II was tried and exiled to Rangoon, where he died in 1862, formally ending Mughal rule.

s: On which date was the East India Company chartered by Elizabeth I?
x: The Company was chartered by Elizabeth I on 31 December 1600; it lost its rule in 1858 and was dissolved in 1874.

s: Under which Act was Queen Victoria proclaimed Empress of India in 1877?
x: The Royal Titles Act, 1876 gave Victoria the title Empress of India; she was proclaimed at the Delhi Durbar on 1 January 1877.

s: Which Viceroy is associated with the Delhi Durbar of 1877, at which Queen Victoria was proclaimed Empress of India?
x: The Empress of India title was proclaimed at Delhi in 1877 under Lytton; Canning read the 1858 Proclamation at Allahabad.

s: The single Indian Army formed in 1895, following the Eden Commission (1879), had how many commands?
x: The Eden Commission recommended abolishing the separate presidency armies; the merged Indian Army of 1895 had four commands, not three.

s: How was the policy of 'divide and counterpoise' reflected in the post-1857 army?
o: Abolition of all regional distinctions in recruitment
Mixing of regiments by caste and region
Replacement of Indian troops by police constables
x: The policy involved mixing regiments by caste and region to prevent unified opposition within the army.

s: After the reorganisation recommended by the Peel Commission, what was the ratio of European to Indian troops?
o: 1:2 in the Bengal Army and 2:5 in the Madras and Bombay armies
2:5 in the Bengal Army and 1:2 in the Madras and Bombay armies
2:1 in the Bengal Army and 5:2 in the Madras and Bombay armies
x: The ratio of European to Indian troops was fixed at 1:2 in the Bengal Army and 2:5 in the Madras and Bombay armies.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the reorganisation of the army after 1857?
o: Regiments were organised without regard to caste or region
Artillery and key positions were reserved for Europeans
Recruitment shifted towards groups described as martial races
Recruitment shifted from Awadh and Bihar towards Punjab, Gorkhas and the NWFP
x: Under 'divide and counterpoise' regiments were deliberately mixed by caste and region, so those identities were not ignored.

s: Which of the following was true of the artillery of the Indian army after the reorganisation of 1859?
o: Shared equally by Europeans and Indians
Handed over to the princely states
x: The Peel Commission kept the artillery exclusively European, barring Indians from heavy weapons.

s:
Consider the following statements about army recruitment after 1857:
1. Recruitment shifted to Gurkhas, Sikhs and Pathans, who had stayed loyal.
2. Recruitment shifted towards Awadh and Bihar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Recruitment shifted to the so-called martial races of Punjab and the NWFP (Gurkhas, Sikhs, Pathans), away from Awadh and Bihar.

s: Which commission reorganised the Indian army in 1859 after the Revolt of 1857?
x: The Peel Commission of 1859 raised the European share and kept the artillery European. The Eden Commission came later, in 1879.

s: Which commission recommended abolishing the separate presidency armies, which led to a single Indian Army in 1895?
x: The Eden Commission (1879) recommended ending the three presidency armies; a single Indian Army with four commands followed in 1895.

s: How did British policy towards Muslims change after 1857?
o: The British transferred all administrative posts exclusively to Muslims.
The British consistently treated Muslims as their principal allies from the beginning.
The British initially blamed and targeted Muslims, but later cultivated them against the educated Hindu middle class.
The British abandoned all communal distinctions and promoted joint political representation.
x: The British initially held Muslims chiefly responsible for the revolt and adopted anti-Muslim measures, but later cultivated Muslim support against the rising educated Hindu middle class.

s: The reversal of the annexation of large estates in Awadh after 1857 resulted in zamindars and taluqdars being granted
o: exclusive authority over the British Indian Army
the right to reject British paramountcy
proprietary rights and transformed into a conservative loyalist class
x: In Awadh, zamindars and taluqdars were restored to proprietary rights and became a conservative and loyal landed class supporting British rule.

s: What were English-educated Indians, viewed with suspicion by the British after 1857, derisively called?
x: Racial arrogance grew after 1857 and English-educated 'Babus' were viewed with suspicion.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about British policy after 1857?
o: Awadh taluqdars were restored to proprietary rights
The reforming zeal of the state was intensified
The state stepped back from missionary activity
x: After 1857 the reforming zeal was abandoned in favour of non-interference, so the third statement is false.

s: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1861, for how long did an ordinance issued by the Viceroy without the council remain valid?
x: The 1861 Act let the Viceroy issue ordinances without the council, valid for six months.

s: Who among the following was NOT one of the first three Indians nominated by Canning to the legislative council in 1862?
x: Canning nominated the Raja of Benares, the Maharaja of Patiala and Sir Dinkar Rao; Lakshmi Narasu Chetty founded the Madras Native Association (1852).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Councils Act, 1861:
1. It reflected the lesson of 1857 that Indians should be associated with law-making.
2. At least half of the additional legislative members were to be non-official.
3. Ordinances issued by the Viceroy were valid for one year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; ordinances under the 1861 Act were valid for six months, not one year.

s: Who introduced the portfolio system in 1859, which was given statutory recognition by the Indian Councils Act, 1861?
x: Canning introduced the portfolio system in 1859, putting each council member in charge of a department; the 1861 Act recognised it.

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Battle of Padmanabham
B. Vellore Mutiny
C. Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy's revolt
D. Rampa rebellion of Tammandora
x: Padmanabham 1794, Vellore 1806, Uyyalawada 1846-47 and Rampa 1879 give A, B, C, D.

s: Who assassinated Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram in his camp after the fall of Bobbili?
x: After Vijayarama Raju, with Bussy's support, took Bobbili from Ranga Rao, Tandra Paparayudu assassinated him in his camp.

s: To whom did the Treaty of Aurangabad of 1753, part of the background to the Battle of Bobbili, give the Circars?
x: The Treaty of Aurangabad of 1753 gave the Circars to the French.

s: The primary source associated with the Battle of Bobbili is which of the following?
x: The play Bobbili Yuddham is identified as the primary source associated with the Battle of Bobbili.

s: Alluri Sitarama Raju fought a direct battle with the British at which place during his Rampa rebellion?
x: During the 1922–24 Rampa rebellion, Alluri Sitarama Raju fought the British directly at Panjerighat.

s: As symbols of what are Ranga Rao and Tandra Paparayudu mainly remembered in Andhra history?
x: Ranga Rao and Tandra Paparayudu of Bobbili remain enduring symbols of Telugu valour.

s: For which region was the Battle of Chandurthi (1758), in which the English defeated the French, fought?
x: The English beat the French at Chandurthi in 1758 in the struggle for the Northern Circars.

s: Which of the following pairs (battle – year) is correctly matched?
x: Padmanabham was fought in 1794; Bobbili was 1757, Chandurthi 1758 and Raichur 1520.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Battle of Palnadu, Nagamma and Nalagama Raju were responsible, and Kakati Rudra Deva helped.
2. The Muthukur Battle was fought between Ganapatideva's Kakatiyas, allied with Manmasiddhi II, and the Pandyan king Jatavarman Sundara Pandya I.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: Both are correct as stated.

s: Which of the following pairs (battle – alternative name) is correctly matched?
o: Battle of Bobbili – Battle of Padmanabha
Battle of Tallikota – Battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi
Battle of Padmanabham – Battle of Palanadu
x: Tallikota is also called the Battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi; Bobbili is the Bobbili-Vizianagaram battle, Padmanabham the Battle of Padmanabha and Palnadu the Battle of Palanadu.

s: After the Battle of Tallikota (1565), to which place did the capital of Vijayanagara shift?
x: Vijayanagara's defeat at Tallikota in 1565 led to the capital moving to Penugonda.

s: With which battle in Andhra is the French commander Bussy associated?
x: In 1757 the French under Bussy helped Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram against Bobbili.

s: Which battle was fought on 24 January 1757?
x: The Battle of Bobbili was fought on 24 January 1757. Padmanabham was in 1794 and Chandurthi in 1758.

s: In which year was the Battle of Chandurthi fought, in which the English defeated the French?
x: The English defeated the French at Chandurthi in 1758, a year after Bobbili, and gained the Northern Circars.

s: Who was the ruler of Bobbili when it was attacked by Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram and the French in 1757?
x: Bobbili was defended by Ranga Rao, whose queen was Mallamma Devi; the fort fell to Vizianagaram and Bussy's French troops.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Bobbili (1757):
1. Bobbili was defended by Ranga Rao.
2. The French under Bussy helped Bobbili against Vizianagaram.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Ranga Rao defended Bobbili; the French under Bussy helped the attacker, Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: The Battle of Raichur (1520) is regarded as the greatest battle of which ruler?
x: Raichur (1520) was the greatest battle of Sri Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara.

s: Which British officer commanded the Company forces at the Battle of Padmanabham?
x: Colonel Pendergast commanded the English East India Company forces at the Battle of Padmanabham.

s: After the British seized the Vizianagaram fort on 2 August 1793, where was the Raja ordered to live?
x: The Raja was ordered to live in Machilipatnam, not Bobbili, after refusing the Rs 3 lakh tribute and disbanding of troops.

s: Where did the minor son Narayana Babu hide before Vizianagaram was restored to him after the Battle of Padmanabham?
x: Narayana Babu had hidden at Makkuva; the estate, reduced to an ordinary zamindari, was restored on accepting the Permanent Settlement (1802) and a Rs 6 lakh peshkash.

s: On which date was the Battle of Padmanabham fought?
x: The Battle of Padmanabham was fought on 10 July 1794; 24 January 1757 is Bobbili and 2 August 1793 the seizure of Vizianagaram fort.

s: After the Battle of Padmanabham, Vizianagaram was restored to Narayana Babu on his accepting the Permanent Settlement and a peshkash of how much?
x: Narayana Babu was restored on accepting the Permanent Settlement (1802) and a Rs 6 lakh peshkash; Rs 3 lakh was the earlier tribute demanded.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Battle of Padmanabham (1794)?
o: It was fought between the Company and Vizianagaram
The Raja and about 1,000 Kshatriya warriors were killed
It ended with Vizianagaram helped by the French defeating Bobbili
Vizianagaram was reduced to an ordinary zamindari
x: Vizianagaram with French help defeating Bobbili is the Battle of Bobbili (1757); Padmanabham was Company vs Vizianagaram.

s: Where is Padmanabham, the site of the battle of 1794, located?
x: The Battle of Padmanabham (10 July 1794) was fought at Padmanabham, between Bhimunipatnam and Vizianagaram.

s: What did the Company demand from Chinna Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram, which led to the Battle of Padmanabham?
o: A tribute of Rs 3 lakh and disbanding of his troops
x: The Company demanded Rs 3 lakh tribute and the disbanding of troops; the Raja refused, and the fight ended at Padmanabham in 1794.

s: Why did the Revolt of 1857 have only a limited impact in South India?
o: The British had withdrawn their forces from the Deccan before 1857
The rulers of all South Indian states openly supported the revolt
The revolts in South India were local and scattered, while the Nizam's loyalty kept the Deccan from joining the revolt
South India had already achieved complete independence from the East India Company
x: The revolts in South India were local and scattered. The Nizam's loyalty to the British also prevented the revolt from spreading across the Deccan.

s: Who among the following was associated with the suppression of the uprising at Paralakimidi in the Ganjam region during the Revolt of 1857?
x: Captain Wilson suppressed the uprising led by Radhakrishna Dandasena at Paralakimidi and Dandasena was subsequently hanged.

s: Korukonda Subba Reddy's rising in the Godavari Agency was influenced by rumours about whose army?
x: Subba Reddy, operating at Errannagudem, was influenced by rumours of Nana Saheb's army; he was captured and executed.

s: On 28 August 1857, what was Sheikh Peer Sahib of Cuddapah reported to have done?
o: attacked the British Residency at Hyderabad
preached jihad and prayed for the success of the Mughal Emperor
raised a green flag at Machilipatnam
x: Sheikh Peer Sahib preached jihad at Cuddapah on 28 August 1857 and prayed for the success of the Mughal Emperor; he was later arrested.

s: Korukonda Subba Reddy, leader of the Godavari Agency movement, was a village official of which place?
x: Korukonda Subba Reddy was the village official of Karaturu in Godavari district. Errannagudem was the centre of his movement.

s: Which of the following statements regarding incidents in the Andhra region during the Revolt of 1857 is correct?
o: A Telugu placard at Visakhapatnam called for renaming the town Mohammed Pattanam.
The treasury at Jaggayyapeta was used to store weapons for the Company.
A green flag was raised at Machilipatnam in support of the British Crown.
The unrest was confined to Visakhapatnam and did not spread to Narsipatnam.
x: A Telugu placard displayed at Visakhapatnam during Muharram called for renaming the town Mohammed Pattanam. The Jaggayyapeta treasury was looted, and unrest also spread to Narsipatnam.

s: Who assisted the British in putting down the rising led by Korukonda Subba Reddy?
x: Buttaigudem Munsab Shankar Swamy helped the British suppress Korukonda Subba Reddy's rising in the Godavari Agency.

s: Radhakrishna Dandasena of Paralakimidi led a 1857 revolt of which tribe?
x: Dandasena led the Savaras of Paralakimidi against the ban on forest produce, not a Godavari Agency rising.

s: During 1857, a treasury was looted at which place in Andhra?
x: The treasury at Jaggayyapeta was looted; a placard at Visakhapatnam called for renaming it Mohammed Pattanam.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Madras Presidency under Crown rule is NOT correctly matched?
o: Madras High Court replaces Company courts – 1858
x: The Madras High Court replaced the Company courts in 1862, not 1858; the Proclamation (1858), IPC (1860) and CrPC (1861) are correct.

s: Which of the following explains the limited response to the Revolt of 1857 in Andhra?
o: Andhra had no local leaders at all
The Nizam had joined the revolt
Andhra was administered directly from London
Many preferred the stability of Company rule to the earlier anarchy
x: Many preferred Company stability to the earlier anarchy, and loyalty meetings were held at Visakhapatnam, Rajahmundry and Vijayawada; local leaders such as Korukonda Subba Reddy did exist.

s: Loyalty meetings for the Company were held in 1857 at Visakhapatnam, Rajahmundry and which other place?
x: Loyalty meetings were held at Visakhapatnam, Rajahmundry and Vijayawada, showing the limited response in Andhra.

s: In which year did the Madras High Court replace the Company courts under Crown rule?
x: The Madras High Court came in 1862, after the Proclamation (1858), IPC (1860) and CrPC (1861).

s:
Assertion (A): The Revolt of 1857 had only a limited impact in Hyderabad State.
Reason (R): The Nizam Afzal-ud-Daula and his Diwan Salar Jung I stayed loyal to the British.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true. The loyalty of the Nizam and Salar Jung kept the Deccan closed to the revolt, so R explains A.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Faujdari Adalat — Centre of the Godavari Agency movement
Korukonda Subba Reddy — Leader in the Godavari Agency
x: The Faujdari Adalat was the court that tried the Uyyalawada rebel leader; it was not the centre of the Godavari Agency movement. Errannagudem was the centre, and Musset Sunkaraswamy was the informer.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gulugonda/Ganjam agency rising — Korra Mallayya and Chinna Bhupathi
x: The Rampa rebellion occurred in 1879, whereas Mubariz-ud-Daula was associated with the 1839 Wahabi conspiracy. Taranikallu, Gulugonda/Ganjam and Uyyalawada are correctly matched with the persons shown.

s: Along with Rampa, in which region did people rise against the forest laws in 1879?
x: The Rampa and Rekapalle rebellions both broke out in 1879 against forest and toddy-tax limits.

s: Which tribe rose in the Rampa rebellion of 1879 in the East Godavari Agency?
x: The 1879 Rampa rising was a Koya uprising against forest and toddy restrictions affecting podu cultivation.

s: Who led the Rampa rebellion of 1879?
x: The 1879 Rampa rebellion was led by Tammandora. Alluri Sitarama Raju led the later Rampa rebellion of 1922–24.

s:
Arrange the following agency disturbances in chronological order:
A. Vizianagaram–Visakhapatnam hill unrest
B. Korra Mallayya and Chinna Bhupathi's movement
C. Korukonda Subba Reddy's movement
D. Rampa rebellion led by Tammandora
x: The correct order is Vizianagaram–Visakhapatnam hill unrest in the 1830s, Korra Mallayya and Chinna Bhupathi in 1845–48, Korukonda Subba Reddy in 1857–58, and the Rampa rebellion in 1879.

s: What was the Rampa rebellion of 1879 mainly against?
o: Limits on podu cultivation and the toddy tax
x: The 1879 Koya rising under Tammandora opposed forest and toddy (chigur) tax limits that hurt podu cultivation.

s: Which tribes mainly supported Alluri Sitarama Raju's rebellion of 1922-24?
x: Alluri's Rampa rebellion drew on the Koya and Konda Dora tribes; the Savaras were Dandasena's followers.

s: Which tribal rising took place in the East Godavari Agency in 1879?
x: The Rampa rebellion of 1879 was a Koya rising led by Tammandora. Alluri's rebellion was in 1922-24.

s: In which year did the Ganjam Agency rising of Korra Mallayya and Chinna Bhupathi begin?
x: Korra Mallayya and Chinna Bhupathi led the Ganjam Agency rising of 1845-48 against plains moneylenders.

s: Who inquired into the causes of the Rampa rebellion of 1879?
x: Sullivan of the Board of Revenue inquired into the 1879 Rampa rising and found the toddy tax and the mansabdar's oppression as causes.

s: The hill unrest of the 1830s in the Vizianagaram-Visakhapatnam region led to the introduction of which system?
x: Unrest against zamindari exactions in the Vizianagaram-Visakhapatnam hills in the 1830s led to the Agency system.

s: In which year were the Nawabs of Kurnool, descended from Golconda nobles, reduced and deposed?
x: The Kurnool Nawabs were reduced and deposed in 1839.

s: In which year was Mubariz-ud-Daula of Hyderabad arrested?
x: Mubariz-ud-Daula was arrested in 1839, long before the Aurangabad outbreak and the Residency attack of 1857.

s: Which of the following sets contains the principal background grievances connected with discontent in Hyderabad State and Andhra before or during 1857?
o: The 1794 battle, the 1846–47 rising and the 1879 Rampa rebellion only
The Permanent Settlement, the Star of India and the restoration of Dharaseo
The 1800 cession, the 1839 Wahabi conspiracy and the 1853 Berar treaty
The 1857 Residency attack, the 1862 conspiracy and the 1801 hanging only
x: The major background grievances identified were the 1800 cession, the Wahabi conspiracy of 1839 and the 1853 Berar treaty, involving Berar, Raichur and Osmanabad/Dharashiv.

s: As a reward for loyalty after 1857, which territories were restored to Hyderabad, along with the writing off of its debt?
x: The Raichur Doab and Dharashiv were restored to Hyderabad and its debt was written off.

s: Which of the following events occurred in 1853?
o: The Residency at Hyderabad was attacked.
x: Opposition to the Berar assignment occurred in 1853. The Residency attack was in 1857, the Rampa rebellion in 1879, and Mubariz-ud-Daula's imprisonment in 1839.

s: For what sum did the Company take Guntur from Nizam Ali in 1788?
x: The Company acquired Guntur from Nizam Ali in 1788 for Rs 7 lakh.

s: Who succeeded Nizam Nasir-ud-Daula in Hyderabad in 1857?
x: Afzal-ud-Daula succeeded Nasir-ud-Daula in 1857 and ruled until 1869.

s: By what name is Mir Turab Ali Khan, the Diwan of Hyderabad during 1857, better known?
x: Afzal-ud-Daula, who succeeded Nasir-ud-Daula on 16 May 1857, retained Mir Turab Ali Khan (Salar Jung I) as Diwan; both were pro-British.

s: Which unit of the Hyderabad Contingent came under suspicion and was disarmed at Aurangabad in June 1857?
x: The 1st Cavalry of the Hyderabad Contingent was suspected and disarmed at Aurangabad; Mir Fida Ali was hanged.

s: What did Turrebaz Khan and Maulvi Allauddin immediately aim to do by attacking the British Residency at Hyderabad?
x: The attack was undertaken to free Jamedar Chida Khan, who had been arrested and held at Hyderabad.

s: Near which place was Turrebaz Khan, who led the attack on the Hyderabad Residency in 1857, later caught and shot?
x: After Resident Davidson repulsed the attack, Turrebaz Khan escaped but was caught and shot near Toopran (1859).

s: Which loyalist received the Star of India after the revolt?
x: Afzal-ud-Daula received the Star of India, while Salar Jung was honoured separately.

s: Which Resident repulsed the attack on the Hyderabad Residency on 17 July 1857?
x: Resident Davidson repulsed the attack by Turrebaz Khan and Maulvi Allauddin.

s: What happened to Maulvi Allauddin after the Residency attack of 1857?
x: Allauddin was sent to the Andamans; Turrebaz Khan was shot near Toopran (1859).

s:
Arrange the following Hyderabad events of 1857 in chronological order:
A. Death of Nizam Nasir-ud-Daula
B. Disarming of the 1st Cavalry at Aurangabad
C. Attack on the Residency by Turrebaz Khan
x: Nasir-ud-Daula died on 16 May 1857, the Aurangabad cavalry was disarmed in June and the Residency was attacked on 17 July 1857.

s: Mubariz-ud-Daula, the brother of the Nizam, led which anti-British movement in 1839?
x: Mubariz-ud-Daula led the Wahabi Movement of 1839; he was arrested and jailed in Golconda Fort.

s: In which fort was Mubariz-ud-Daula, the leader of the Wahabi Movement of 1839, imprisoned?
x: Mubariz-ud-Daula, the Nizam's brother, was arrested and jailed in Golconda Fort.

s: Who led the revolt at Aurangabad in June 1857?
x: At Aurangabad the 1st Cavalry of the Hyderabad Contingent was disarmed and Mir Fida Ali revolted; Captain Abbot suppressed it and Fida Ali was hanged.

s: Who led the rising against the British at Shorapur in 1858?
x: In 1858 Raja Venkatappa Nayaka of Shorapur rose against the British, the last of the Hyderabad-region risings in order.

s: In 1858, Raja Venkatappa Nayaka rose against the British at which place?
x: Venkatappa Nayaka was the Raja of Shorapur; his rising of 1858 came after the Hyderabad Residency attack of 1857.

s: Which of the following pairs (leader – place or event of 1857) is correctly matched?
o: Turrebaz Khan – Attack on the British Residency
Korukonda Subba Reddy – Imprisoned in Golconda Fort
x: Turrebaz Khan attacked the British Residency; Dandasena rose at Paralakimidi, Subba Reddy led at Errannagudem and Mubariz-ud-Daula was imprisoned in Golconda Fort.

s: Whom did the Residency attack of 17 July 1857 aim to free?
x: Turrebaz Khan and Maulvi Allauddin attacked the Residency to free the arrested Jamedar Chida Khan.

s:
Consider the following statements about zamindari resistance to the Company:
1. The zamindars of Ghumsur in Ganjam resisted the Company.
2. The resistance at Parlakimedi was a revolt by the Nizam's army.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Ghumsur's zamindars resisted the Company; Parlakimedi's resistance too was by zamindars, not the Nizam's army.

s: Of which estate was Narasimha Appa Rao, who opposed Company control, the zamindar?
x: Narasimha Appa Rao of Nuzvid resisted the Company, which finally partitioned the estate.

s: In which year did Bhupayya, who led about 2,000 followers in the Vizag hills against the Company, die?
x: Bhupayya was driven into the Nizam's territory and died in 1796.

s: Which development adversely affected the traditional rights of the Poligars in the Carnatic and Tirunelveli region?
o: The introduction of Ryotwari settlement in 1847
The Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam in 1798 alone
The recall of William Bentinck from Madras
The Company's 1781 arrangement allowing the Nawab of Arcot to manage revenue
x: The Company's 1781 arrangement allowed the Nawab of Arcot to manage the revenues of Tirunelveli and the Carnatic, affecting the rights of the Poligars.

s: In which year was Veerapandya Kattabomman hanged?
x: Kattabomman was hanged in 1799; the Marudu brothers were executed in 1801.

s: What was the principal cause of the Vellore Mutiny?
o: The Company's takeover of Guntur from the Nizam
The introduction of Ryotwari settlement in the Ceded Districts
Confiscation of the estates of the Marudu brothers
New dress regulations that offended caste and religious sentiments
x: The new uniform regulations, including changes concerning the turban and a ban on caste marks, hurt the caste and religious sentiments of the sepoys.

s: From where did the Marudu brothers, executed at Tiruppathur in 1801, lead the South Indian Rebellion?
x: The Marudu brothers of Sivaganga led the South Indian Rebellion; Panchalankurichi was Kattabomman's.

s: Who issued the Kundara Proclamation of 11 January 1809?
x: Velu Thampi Dalawa, Diwan of Travancore, issued the Kundara Proclamation during his 1808-09 revolt, not Munro.

s: Veerapandya Kattabomman was the poligar of which place?
x: Kattabomman was the poligar of Panchalankurichi in Tirunelveli; he was hanged at Kayattar in 1799.

s: Which consequence followed the Vellore Mutiny?
o: The Agency system was abolished immediately.
Thomas Munro was appointed Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts.
Mubariz-ud-Daula was released from Golconda Fort.
Madras Governor William Bentinck and Commander-in-Chief Cradock were recalled.
x: Following the mutiny, Madras Governor William Bentinck and the Commander-in-Chief Cradock were recalled.

s: When did the Vellore Mutiny break out?
x: The sepoys seized Vellore Fort on 10 July 1806, half a century before 1857.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Vellore Mutiny:
1. New dress regulations banning caste marks were a cause.
2. Tipu's family was lodged in Vellore Fort.
3. It came after the Revolt of 1857.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Dress regulations and the presence of Tipu's family were causes; the 1806 mutiny was the first big sepoy mutiny, before 1857.

s: Which was the first big sepoy mutiny in India, about half a century before 1857?
x: The Vellore Mutiny of 10 July 1806 was the first big sepoy mutiny, caused by new dress rules and the presence of Tipu's family in the fort.

s: Who were the palegars of the Ceded Districts?
o: British civil servants appointed by the Madras Governor
Religious heads controlling the Wahabi Movement
Fortified military chiefs exercising autonomous power under the Nizam's nominal suzerainty
x: Palegars were fortified military chiefs who exercised autonomous power under the nominal suzerainty of the Nizam.

s: Who captured and hanged Mutakuri Goudappa, who attacked the Sub-Collector's office at Taranikallu in 1801?
x: Goudappa was captured and hanged by Sub-Collector Dhakar, not by Collector Thomas Munro.

s: Which of the following was NOT among the principal causes of resistance by Palegars and other local groups?
o: The Company's order to disarm the Palegars
The introduction of the Kundara Proclamation by Thomas Munro
Forfeiture of estates under the Permanent Settlement
x: Heavy revenue and peshkash demands, estate forfeiture and the order to disarm Palegars were causes of resistance. The Kundara Proclamation was associated with Velu Thampi, not Thomas Munro's Palegar policy.

s: In which year did the Nizam cede Cuddapah, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary to the Company?
x: The Ceded Districts were handed over in 1800 under the Subsidiary Alliance of 1798; Guntur had been taken in 1788 for Rs 7 lakh.

s: Who was the principal officer responsible for suppressing the Palegar revolts in the Ceded Districts?
x: Thomas Munro, serving as Principal Collector, was chiefly responsible for suppressing the Palegar revolts.

s: For about how long did military action to suppress the Palegars continue?
x: Suppression combined disarmament proclamations, eighteen months of military action, confiscation of rebel estates and small pensions for loyal heirs.

s: Which settlement was introduced in the Ceded Districts after the suppression of the Palegars?
x: The settlement introduced in the Ceded Districts was Ryotwari. Permanent Settlement is an incorrect attribution in this context.

s: What was the immediate cause of Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy's revolt?
o: A ban on podu cultivation and toddy tapping
Takeover of his estate, reduction to a meagre pension, and the order to disarm and pay peshkash
Introduction of new military uniforms at Vellore
Forcible conversion of local chiefs to Christianity
x: His estate was taken over under Munro, he was offered only a meagre pension, and he was ordered to lay down arms and pay peshkash.

s: About how many palegars resisted Thomas Munro in the Ceded Districts in 1800-01?
x: About 80 palegars resisted Munro's order to disarm and pay peshkash.

s: Under which arrangement did the Nizam cede Cuddapah, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary to the Company in 1800?
x: The Ceded Districts were handed over in 1800 under the Nizam's Subsidiary Alliance of 1798.

s: Which group formed the support base of Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy's revolt?
o: Only officials from the Godavari Agency
Farmers, Yanadis, tribal people and people of the Uyyalawada and Nosam estates
Only zamindars from Parlakimedi and Ghumsur
Sepoys of the Madras Army alone
x: The movement had about 5,000 followers, including farmers, Yanadis, tribal people and people from the Uyyalawada and Nosam estates.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the palegar risings in Rayalaseema?
o: The 1846 rising was the last major palegar rising before 1857
Thomas Munro was associated with suppressing the 1800–01 rising
The 1846 rising was led jointly by about 80 palegars
x: About 80 palegars were involved in 1800–01; the 1846 rising was a single-leader guerrilla revolt with a peasant and tribal base.

s: After the 2022 district reorganisation, in which district is Uyyalawada located?
x: After the 2022 reorganisation, Uyyalawada falls in Nandyal district.

s: Who was the maternal grandfather of Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy?
x: He was the younger son of Pedda Mallareddy, Palegar of Uyyalawada, and the maternal grandson of Nosam Palegar Jayarama Reddy.

s: On which date was Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy publicly hanged at Koilakuntla?
x: Captured on 7 October 1846 and sentenced to death by the Faujdari Adalat in January 1847, he was publicly hanged near Koilakuntla on 22 February 1847. 22 February 1846 is a year too early (the revolt began only in July 1846), and 10 July 1806 is the Vellore Mutiny.

s: Where was the leader of the 1846 revolt captured on 7 October 1846?
x: He was captured at the Jagannatha Swamy temple, Pairamalla Konda; Mundlapadu was the ambush site and Rudravaram and Koilakuntla were looted.

s: After whom has Orvakal airport in Kurnool, operational from 25 March 2021, been named?
x: Orvakal airport was renamed Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy Airport.

s: Who raised the alarm regarding the revolt associated with Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy?
x: Kadapa Collector J. H. Cockrane raised the alarm. Captain Nott, Captain Russell and Lieutenant Moore were deployed subsequently.

s: After his family's estate was taken under Munro, what pension was given to Narasimha Reddy and his brothers?
x: The three sons got a meagre pension of Rs 35; Rs 1,200 was the Vizianagaram Raja's pension.

s: On 12 July 1846, Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy looted Rudravaram and the treasury of which place?
x: On 12 July 1846 he looted Rudravaram and the Koilakuntla treasury.

s: Who ambushed Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy's rebels at Mundlapadu on 24 July 1846?
x: Captain Nott ambushed the rebels at Mundlapadu, killing 25; Wilson suppressed Dandasena and Abbot the Aurangabad outbreak.

s: Which court sentenced Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy to death in January 1847?
x: The Faujdari Adalat tried him for rebellion, murder and looting; its trial record and the Kadapa Collector's reports are the main official records.

s: What is the title of the 2019 film on the Rayalaseema palegar Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy?
x: Sye Raa Narasimha Reddy (2019) commemorates him; Bobbili Yuddham is a play on the 1757 battle.

s: Before the 2022 reorganisation of districts, Uyyalawada, the home of Narasimha Reddy, was in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy belonged to the Palegar family of Uyyalawada in Koilakuntla taluk of Kurnool district. Since the 2022 reorganisation Uyyalawada is in Nandyal district.

s: Which of the following is the main official record of Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy's revolt?
x: The Kadapa Collector's reports and the Faujdari Adalat trial record are the main official records of the 1846-47 revolt.

s: Who conferred the title 'Raja' on Rammohan Roy and sent him to England as his envoy?
x: The Mughal emperor Akbar II gave Rammohan Roy the title 'Raja' and sent him to England as his envoy.

s: Which one of the following titles is NOT associated with Raja Rammohan Roy?
x: Rammohan Roy is called the Father of Modern India, the Father of the Indian (or Bengal) Renaissance and the first Modern Man of India. 'Maharishi' was the title of Debendranath Tagore. 'Raja' was given to Rammohan Roy by Akbar II.

s: While respecting the traditional philosophies of the East, what did Raja Rammohan Roy want Indians to adopt?
o: A rejection of all Eastern thought
x: He drew on the Upanishads and Vedanta while standing for a rational, scientific approach.

s: Where did Raja Rammohan Roy die in 1833?
